analysis: Integration pass over the SSD retirement slicing change. The integration source now includes the removeInSlices implementation (SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift, new lines ~24-47), which resolves the earlier open questions. It loops in slices of filesPerSlice=16 and calls retire(slice). A nil return breaks the loop, so the first refusal ends the batch and earlier results are returned. Results merge correctly: removed is unioned, indexedBytesFreed summed, externalChange OR-ed. An empty batch makes one call, which yields an empty Result, the same as the old nil path. Both callers (SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Maintenance.swift:34-41 and SSDPrefixCache.swift ~1794-1801) now take removalLock per slice and re-evaluate hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot each time, then call SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove, which still goes through the epoch barrier (performOwnedRetirement). Per-file protections are unchanged: exact-path guard, no-wait lease, no-follow status and index checks. If ownership is lost mid-batch, later slices are not unlinked. The new tests (SSDOwnedEntryRetirementTests lines 105-151) cover 16/16/8 slicing, a refused slice stopping the batch with later files left on disk, and the empty batch. No change to T-041 controls: HMAC-keyed names, AES-GCM/DBK3, 30-minute TTL, disk budget, KEK purge, salt scoping, or the SEC-035 accepted risk. Shorter lock holds improve availability (cache-hit submit thread, donor publication). Residual non-atomicity across slices lets concurrent donors or reads interleave; the code already tolerates this through per-file leases, forgetMissing and removeStaleBlock. A slice that fails ownership leaves the remaining expired files for a later sweep, which is a bounded fail-safe and not a new exposure. The changelog and docs edits match the code. Not verified: the body of SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove and performOwnedRetirement (not changed here), and 23 omitted replay units. No security regression is evident.
